text:
sam: quick q — we're running some internal infra jobs and want to disable client telemetry from the python sdk (no metrics, no user-agent), but still keep trace propagation into our opentelemetry traces. any recommended flags or patterns?

maria: short answer: yes. two layers — (1) disable sending client metrics, (2) control user-agent header, (3) keep W3C tracecontext propagation (traceparent) untouched. in py sdk we added a small config for this: 

maria: example: 
```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., telemetry={"send_metrics": False, "user_agent": None, "propagate_tracing": True})
# or via env: REDWOOD_SEND_METRICS=false REDWOOD_USER_AGENT=
```

maria: notes: setting user_agent to None will omit the SDK user-agent addition and not append extra identifying info. send_metrics=False prevents the background metrics pings and per-request metric labels.

alex: does send_metrics=False also stop the per-request latency counter for streaming (we have long-lived streams)?

maria: good call — streaming has a slightly different lifecycle. metrics are emitted when the request finishes or the stream is closed. for truly long-lived streams, call `await client._telemetry.flush()` on shutdown (we currently expose a `flush()` helper). we'll add a public method if necessary.

maria: for tracing: we follow W3C tracecontext. if an incoming HTTP request has a `traceparent` header we forward it unchanged. if there's none and `propagate_tracing` is True, the SDK will add a `traceparent` header from the active OpenTelemetry span (if otel is present). so you can keep full continuity.

maria: header examples (what we set):
```
traceparent: 00-4bf92f3577b34da6a3ce929d0e0e4736-00f067aa0ba902b7-01
user-agent: redwood-sdk-python-1.4.2 (dedicated)
```

sam: perfect. is there an env var to flip for CI/jobs so we don't have to change code everywhere?

maria: yes — we support REDWOOD_SEND_METRICS=false and REDWOOD_USER_AGENT="" (empty) to suppress UA. REDWOOD_PROPAGATE_TRACING=true/false toggles trace propagation. these are read at client init.

alex: what about node/js SDK differences? streaming/quic behavior?

maria: node is similar. JS client config uses `telemetry: { enabled: false, userAgent: null, propagateTracing: true }`. note: due to streaming using fetch/ReadableStream, some older runtimes don't forward incoming headers automatically; in server-side node we explicitly copy `traceparent` from incoming request to the outbound fetch. in edge runtimes that auto-propagate you should be fine.

alex: ok will add a one-liner in the docs. can we get a small sample snippet for the quickstart page?

maria: i'll open a PR with the sample and a short note about long-lived streams + flush. cc @alex for review.

sdk-bot: test-runner: python unit tests for telemetry toggles passed (telemetry:tests::test_disable_metrics) :white_check_mark:

sam: awesome, thanks. if you can also add a note in the migration guide about the `user_agent` empty-string behavior that'd help support triage.

maria: on it, adding to docs + changelog entry.

sam: thanks all :party-parrot:
